questions.stem_markdown: At the start of a comprehensive adolescent alcohol and drug assessment in a Sydney clinic, a 16-year-old says she will only continue if the clinician explains how private the discussion is. Which response best matches the notes?

Explain confidentiality early as part of engagement before continuing the assessment
Ask the parent to answer the sensitive questions first so the adolescent does not feel pressured
Avoid discussing confidentiality because it may make the young person less honest
Limit the review to physical symptoms until the family decides whether confidentiality is appropriate

questions.explanation_markdown: The notes list **engagement and discussion of confidentiality** as part of a comprehensive adolescent drug and alcohol assessment. That makes early explanation of confidentiality the best way to maintain engagement before proceeding with more sensitive questions.

why_others_wrong.A: The source material places discussion of confidentiality within the assessment rather than only after a problem is identified.
why_others_wrong.C: The notes do not say the parent should answer the sensitive parts of the assessment on the adolescent’s behalf.
why_others_wrong.D: The source material supports discussing confidentiality, not avoiding it.
why_others_wrong.E: The notes frame confidentiality discussion as part of the assessment process rather than a reason to stop the consultation.

key_takeaways: The notes explicitly include discussion of confidentiality in comprehensive adolescent AOD assessment.
Early explanation of confidentiality supports engagement.
Sensitive adolescent assessment is better when expectations are set clearly at the start.
